cases.context: A mid-sized retailer must choose one forecasting software vendor for a six-month pilot. The operations team has no predetermined weighting rule. All six factors must be considered, and either option could be reasonable.
cases.question: For this six-month pilot, should the retailer select Option A or Option B?

factors.text: Security: A holds a current independent security certification; B has not completed an external security audit.
factors.edit_a: Security: B holds a current independent security certification; A has not completed an external security audit.
factors.edit_b: Security: An outside auditor has certified B, while A currently lacks external certification.

factors.text: Price: A charges 30 percent more than B for the six-month pilot, with otherwise identical billing terms.
factors.edit_a: Price: B charges 30 percent more than A for the six-month pilot, with otherwise identical billing terms.
factors.edit_b: Price: A is the lower-priced option; B's six-month quote is 30 percent higher on comparable billing terms.

factors.text: Integration: B can connect to the existing inventory system in two weeks; A requires ten weeks of custom integration.
factors.edit_a: Integration: A can connect to the existing inventory system in two weeks; B requires ten weeks of custom integration.
factors.edit_b: Integration: The existing inventory system will work with A after two weeks, but B needs ten weeks of custom integration.

factors.text: Reliability: A has documented 99.95 percent monthly uptime; B has documented 99.0 percent monthly uptime.
factors.edit_a: Reliability: B has documented 99.95 percent monthly uptime; A has documented 99.0 percent monthly uptime.
factors.edit_b: Reliability: Historical monthly availability is 99.95 percent for B but only 99.0 percent for A.

factors.text: Data portability: B allows a full export to an open format at contract end; A charges extra and offers a proprietary export.
factors.edit_a: Data portability: A allows a full export to an open format at contract end; B charges extra and offers a proprietary export.
factors.edit_b: Data portability: At exit, A provides an open-standard export without surcharge, while B provides a proprietary export for an extra fee.

factors.text: Support: A guarantees a staffed 24-hour response team; B only provides weekday business-hours support.
factors.edit_a: Support: B guarantees a staffed 24-hour response team; A only provides weekday business-hours support.
factors.edit_b: Support: B offers round-the-clock staffed assistance, while A's support operates only on weekdays during office hours.

cases.context: A food distributor must choose a delivery method for a regular weekly shipment. Option A is direct refrigerated road transport. Option B is refrigerated intermodal rail plus short road pickup. The dispatcher must weigh the facts without a fixed scoring formula.
cases.question: For the coming weekly shipments, should the distributor choose Option A or Option B?

factors.text: Transit time: A delivers in 18 hours, while B delivers in 42 hours under the current schedule.
factors.edit_a: Transit time: B delivers in 18 hours, while A delivers in 42 hours under the current schedule.
factors.edit_b: Transit time: The current timetable gives B an 18-hour delivery time but A a 42-hour delivery time.

factors.text: Cost: B costs 25 percent less per shipment than A, including transfer and pickup.
factors.edit_a: Cost: A costs 25 percent less per shipment than B, including transfer and pickup.
factors.edit_b: Cost: After all fees, the distributor pays one-quarter less per shipment using A than B.

factors.text: Temperature monitoring: A reports sensor readings continuously; B reports temperature only at two transfer checkpoints.
factors.edit_a: Temperature monitoring: B reports sensor readings continuously; A reports temperature only at two transfer checkpoints.
factors.edit_b: Temperature monitoring: Sensors stream throughout the B shipment, while A provides only two scheduled checkpoint readings.

factors.text: Emissions: B has independently estimated 45 percent lower shipment emissions than A.
factors.edit_a: Emissions: A has independently estimated 45 percent lower shipment emissions than B.
factors.edit_b: Emissions: An external analysis estimates that A emits 45 percent less per shipment than B.

factors.text: Delay variance: A has an observed 5 percent late-arrival rate; B has an observed 18 percent late-arrival rate.
factors.edit_a: Delay variance: B has an observed 5 percent late-arrival rate; A has an observed 18 percent late-arrival rate.
factors.edit_b: Delay variance: In recent dispatch records, only 5 percent of B deliveries were late, compared with 18 percent for A.

factors.text: Capacity: B guarantees space for seasonal demand spikes; A offers the regular weekly volume but no extra capacity guarantee.
factors.edit_a: Capacity: A guarantees space for seasonal demand spikes; B offers the regular weekly volume but no extra capacity guarantee.
factors.edit_b: Capacity: Peak-season extra volume is contractually reserved on A; B commits only to the normal weekly quantity.
